rendered:
They didn't. The optimum the paper picks is 165 μM 4-MPBA[1], not the value in your question. It states that a 4-MPBA concentration of 165 μM was chosen as the optimized condition for all subsequent experiments[2].

The value in your question appears only as the top of the first test range. The CD signal at the probe's main band rose sharply as the 4-MPBA concentration was tuned from 0 to 120 μM[3]. The reasons given for choosing the higher concentration are:
1. Stability: the 165 μM 4-MPBA-derived BA@L-HGNRs showing exceptional spectral stability during the entire monitoring process[4] in NH4HCO3 buffer.
2. CD signal strength: The CD intensity reached its maximum at 165 μM, after which it exhibited a slight decrease at higher concentrations[5]. Going up to 225 μM[6] changed the CD signal only slightly.
